summary: Configured node1 to route auth/authpriv events exclusively to /var/log/auth-events.log while retaining normal system logging. Verified correct routing before and after a full node restart.
actions_performed: Created /etc/rsyslog.d/30-auth-events.conf with auth/authpriv routing and stop semantics.
Confirmed ordinary user-facility events continue reaching /var/log/syslog.
Safely restarted node1 and verified configuration, services, and retained data recovered.

evidence.requirement: Route authentication and authorization messages to /var/log/auth-events.log
evidence.summary: Shows the persistent auth/authpriv rule, successful configuration validation, and live auth/authpriv probes reaching only the dedicated log before and after restart.
Ordinary user-facility probes reached /var/log/syslog, remained absent from the dedicated auth log, and rsyslog plus journald were active.

Captures the healthy baseline with boot ID cd201c7e-7a27-4b28-a631-737e59cba357, safe reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 0b343e86-8287-4ceb-b9a8-79b76d9b7cb4, recovered services and retained data, and successful post-restart routing tests.
